Resolves #19955

`GridHorizontalScrollSync` now keeps the horizontal scrollbar as the single source in both directions. Before, when focus landed on a header outside the centre clip (for example Tab onto a header's menu trigger), the browser scrolled the centre header toolbar by itself. The scrollbar and the body stayed put, so every centre header sat over another column's cells. A filtered column then reads as unfiltered, one reading of the outside report in defect-note `4aa7bdd6`.

The addon now routes such a native header scroll into the scrollbar, so the body follows and the focused column comes into view. It ignores the echo of its own header writes. Comparing against the scrollbar's current value instead would pull a scrollbar that moved again back to the older position.

Evidence: L3 (local Chromium e2e on the issues showcase: red on base, green at head) → L3 required (AC-3).

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | CI-covered: `IssuesShowcase.spec.mjs`, "a header focused outside the centre clip brings its column along (#19955)" asserts `synced` (the centre header toolbar's `scrollLeft` equals the scrollbar's) after focusing the Area menu trigger at 800×600. |
| AC-2 | The same arm asserts `scrolled` (the focus moved the centre header) together with `aligned` (the Area header's left edge within 1 px of its first visible cell), so the focused column is in view with its own cells beneath it. |
| AC-3 | Outside-CI receipt under Test Evidence: base red, head green. |

## Deltas from ticket

- **The echo guard:** the addon records what its own `onScroll` wrote to the header and routes only header scrolls that differ from it. The ticket's "equal values must not echo back" compared values only, and that would race a scrollbar that moved again before the header's scroll event fired.
- **Touched code brought to the file's bar:** the touched methods and the class carry `@summary` JSDoc, and a whitespace-only line in `register` is gone.

## Test Evidence

Local headless Chromium, `playwright.config.e2e.mjs`, this checkout:

- **Base (addon reverted, new arm kept):** the arm fails with `{aligned: false, scrolled: true, synced: false}`. The focus scrolled the header and nothing followed.
- **Head `76c51c1357`:** the arm passed 3/3 (`--repeat-each=3`), and the whole `IssuesShowcase.spec.mjs` passed 9/9.
- **Engine-only `grid/` folder:** 203/203, including the column-drag, overdrag-scroll and header-rect specs. That run was at the fix before the JSDoc-only and whitespace edits.
- **Brain-gated grid specs:** not run locally; this PR's E2E (Brain-gated tier) runs them.
- **Live reproduction before the fix:** on https://neomjs.com/dist/production/examples/grid/issues/index.html (13.3.0, 800×600), tabbing onto "Filter Area" left the centre header at `scrollLeft` 289 while the scrollbar stayed at 0.

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] After the next release, the live showcase at 800×600 keeps every header over its own cells after Tab onto a header's menu trigger.

Routing native centre-header scrolls (`onHeaderScroll`) into `scrollerNode.scrollLeft` while ignoring `onScroll`'s own echo via `registration.headerScrollLeft` keeps the horizontal scrollbar, `.neo-grid-body` (`--grid-scroll-left`), and `ScrollManager#onContainerScroll` aligned when keyboard focus lands on an off-screen header or menu trigger.

**Peer-Review Opening:** 🖖 Sharp root-cause isolation from the 13.3.0 showcase feedback, Ada. Tabbing into a centre header or menu trigger outside the clip caused the browser to scroll `.neo-grid-header-toolbar` independently of `.neo-grid-horizontal-scrollbar`, leaving every centre header label over the wrong column's cells. Forwarding foreign header scrolls into `scrollerNode.scrollLeft` inside `GridHorizontalScrollSync` while guarding against `onScroll` echo via `registration.headerScrollLeft` is clean and minimal.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge OR documented search (per guide §7.1):**

- **Challenge**: In `src/main/addon/GridHorizontalScrollSync.mjs:48-55`, `onHeaderScroll` sets `scrollerNode.scrollLeft = scrollLeft` without immediately updating `registration.headerScrollLeft = scrollerNode.scrollLeft`, relying on `scrollerNode`'s subsequent `scroll` event (`onScroll`) to update `registration.headerScrollLeft`. In normal operation `scrollerNode`'s `scroll` event fires on the next frame and updates both `--grid-scroll-left` and `registration.headerScrollLeft`. The only edge case where `scrollerNode` would not fire a `scroll` event is if `scrollerNode.scrollLeft` was already equal to `scrollLeft` while `registration.headerScrollLeft` held a stale value — which cannot occur as long as `scrollerNode` is only mutated while registered with `onScroll`. Non-blocking.
